newsitem.title: GERMANY: Chinese 97/98 oilseeds crops put at 39.9 mln T.
newsitem.headline: Chinese 97/98 oilseeds crops put at 39.9 mln T.

text.p: Chinese oilseeds crops in 1997/98 are forecast at 39.9 million tonnes, up from an estimated 38.0 million in 96/97, the Oil World newsletter said.

The independent publication cited increases in the major crops -- soybeans, rapeseed and cottonseed -- but said the result would be below 41.3 million achieved in 95/96 and therefore made higher imports of oils and fats necessary.

It pegged Chinese imports of oils and fats in 97/98 (soy oil, cotton oil, groundnut oil, rape oil, lard, tallow/grease and others) at five million tonnes in 97/98, compared with an estimated 4.16 million in 96/97 and 3.31 million in 95/96.
China's domestic output of oils and fats was put at 10.5 million tonnes in 97/98 (10.3 million 96/97) and consumption at 15 million tonnes in 97/98 (14.3 million in 96/97).
Per-capita consumption of oils/fats was seen rising on income growth to 12.2 kilos in 97/98 from 11.7 kilos in 96/97.
The world average use of oils and fats is 16.8 kilos.

Oil World also saw China's oilmeal imports rising along with growing meat demand. It put 97/98 meal imports (soymeal, cotton meal, groundnutmeal, rape meal) at 5.4 million tonnes, up from 4.4 million in 96/97 and 2.4 million in 95/96.
